name: Frank Keeler
role: Company store clerk; later brick-kiln operator at Livingston
bio: Frank Keeler filled George Porter's place at the company store in early 1884 and was again helping hold down a store in October 1885. In April 1884 he and John Goodall gave the stockmen's ball, and he signed the call for that month's Republican county convention. His son was born April 11, 1885, and in May Mrs. Keeler and the baby joined him in Medora; that spring he and Martin panned for gold up the river. In March 1886 he was bringing beef in from down the river, and by July 1886 he had set up a brick kiln at Livingston.

An interesting wager was decided the first of the week between Wm. Vandriesche and Frank Keeler. William was to ride the bucker spoken of in another article, for half an hour. He won the bet but at the expense of a tumble or two.
Frank Keeler received as a Christmas present from Duncan & Hillis, of Mandan, a fine arm-chair, that is a decided addition to Frank's "boudoir."
Frank Keeler returned from Mandan Sunday, where he went to see his wife.

If present indications hold out, Medora will soon have a gold mine craze. Messrs. Martin and Keeler recently panned out about twenty cents in one pan of dirt up the river. This is excellent pay and if it holds out will make first class diggings.
